## Highlights

- OpenAI gateway accounts now recover from revoked access-token generations without
  reusing rejected credentials. A late usage response cannot overwrite a terminal
  refresh refusal, so an affected account stays out of the shared pool until a
  new generation is available. Generic usage failures keep their existing retry
  behavior. [#4664](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4664),
  [#4667](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4667)
- `tale deploy observe` now keeps its retained-state checks and refusal phases
  bounded to read-only evidence, including portable lock and native-artifact
  validation. Observation never applies deployment changes or certifies readiness.
  [#4648](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4648),
  [#4655](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4655),
  [#4657](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4657),
  [#4660](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4660),
  [#4662](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4662)
- CLI release checks now include every command suite, keep hashed workflow sources
  byte-stable on Windows, and reject receipt symlinks on platforms without
  `O_NOFOLLOW`. This prevents a platform-specific release from silently skipping
  a CLI suite or accepting a redirected receipt. [#4668](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4668)

## Upgrade notes

- Deploy the Tale platform and CLI together before adopting these fixes.
  Managed deployments use the shared Tale CLI source from `13a41556`.
- No database migration is included in this release. Keep the existing backup,
  retained-release and configuration readback procedure, and verify the gateway
  account state after rollout before sending new task turns.
